slides.title: Qwen2.5 0.5B Instruct
slides.body: The smallest member of the Qwen2.5 family. Downloads in seconds and compiles fast, making it the ideal smoke-test and demo model.

cards.label: Great for
cards.text: Use this when you want a fast local sandbox: UI demos, notebook labs, API integration tests, or teaching the OpenAI chat protocol without waiting on a large download.

cards.label: Think twice for
cards.text: Do not expect strong multi-step reasoning or complex coding — graduate to 1.5B/3B for that.

slides.title: What's special?
slides.body: Qwen2.5 pushed small-model quality by pretraining on ~18T tokens with aggressive data filtering, then applying the same post-training recipe (supervised finetuning + multi-stage reinforcement learning) used by the flagship models. The surprising result: even a 0.5B checkpoint keeps 32K context and usable instruction following — proof that data quality and post-training transfer down the size ladder.
bullets: Small models can inherit the post-training recipe of larger siblings
Long context (32K) is no longer reserved for huge models
Instruction tuning matters as much as raw parameter count at this size

slides.title: Inside the model
slides.body: Dense decoder-only transformer (Qwen2 architecture): grouped-query attention (GQA), SwiGLU feed-forward layers, RoPE positional embeddings, and a large vocabulary (~150k) tokenizer that helps multilingual and code performance. The Instruct variant is chat-tuned with a ChatML-style template.

flow.caption: Attention gathers context; the feed-forward layers transform it; the cycle repeats one token at a time.

steps.label: Prompt
steps.text: Your chat messages become token ids.

steps.label: Attention
steps.text: Each token looks back at useful context.

steps.label: MLP
steps.text: A dense feed-forward block transforms the state.

steps.label: Next token
steps.text: Sample / argmax → stream the next piece of text.

slides.title: One token through the stack
slides.body: Generation is a loop: build context, run the transformer block stack, sample the next token, append, repeat.
bullets: Prefill reads the prompt once; decode emits one token at a time
KV cache remembers attention state so decode stays cheap
Temperature / top_p only change the final sampling step

slides.title: Talk to the local server
slides.body: After Serve shows running, the notebook uses the same OpenAI-compatible API that Chat uses — no cloud round-trip.
slides.code:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8100/v1",
    api_key="local",  # ignored by max serve
)
stream = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Explain this model in one sentence."}],
    stream=True,
    max_tokens=64,
)
for event in stream:
    delta = event.choices[0].delta.content or ""
    print(delta, end="", flush=True)

steps.label: Point the client
steps.text: base_url is mxstudio's max serve port (8100).

steps.label: Send one chat turn
steps.text: Use the Hugging Face id as the model name.

steps.label: Stream tokens
steps.text: Each event carries a tiny delta — that is generation you can feel.
